answer: When a comet sinks to its nadir over the observatory, a claimant climbs to the dome and photographs the comet through the sighting ring of the brass relic astrolabe, date and position both legible, timestamped and witnessed beside the dome log. Two keepers check the photograph against the comet's ephemeris and the dome log within five days. A copied photo, wrong position, or missing log entry voids the season, burns a 60-credit stake, and bars the sponsor for a year. One honest climber spends 60 credits; a thousand fakes would need a thousand night climbs and a thousand real photographs.
